---
title: "Shortcode reference"
---

*Reference: [CLI](cli.qmd) · [Front matter](frontmatter.qmd) · [Cell options](cell-options.qmd) · [Configuration](configuration.qmd) · Shortcodes · [Troubleshooting](troubleshooting.qmd)*

A shortcode is a `{{< name args >}}` tag in the body of a document. qmd-fast
expands the built-in shortcodes (and any an extension declares) in a single pass
**before** the Markdown is parsed, so the result is just HTML or Markdown by the
time comrak sees it. Two rules keep that pass from surprising you:

- **Code is sacred.** A `{{< … >}}` inside a fenced block (```` ``` ````) or an
  inline code span (`` `…` ``) is left exactly as written, so every example on this
  page is a real, unexpanded shortcode rather than a thing that quietly ran. That is
  also why you can document a shortcode in prose without arming it.
- **Unknown is loud, not silent.** A `{{< … >}}` whose name no built-in and no
  active extension declares is left in the page verbatim **and** reported as a
  located diagnostic, so a typo shows up in the dev menu, the
  build log, and `qmd-fast check` rather than shipping as literal text. The one
  exception is `{{< include >}}`, which an earlier pass resolves and reports on its
  own (see below), so it is never double-warned.

Expansion is line-preserving: each shortcode opens and closes on one line and
expands inline, so click-to-source still points at the right line.

There are four built-in shortcodes, documented below, plus the
[extension-declared](#extension-declared-shortcodes) shortcodes any active
extension contributes.

## `{{< include >}}`: inline a partial

```markdown
{{< include path/to/partial.qmd >}}
```

Splices another file's contents into this one **before** parsing, as if you had
pasted it in place. The directive must be alone on its own line (leading and
trailing whitespace is fine); a `{{< include … >}}` with other text on the line is
left as ordinary content. The path is resolved relative to the file that holds the
directive, so a partial can itself include further partials and the relative paths
still make sense at each level.

Includes are how you keep one author bio, one license footer, or one shared figure
in a single file and pull it into many pages. Because the splice happens before the
block model is built, the included blocks are first-class: they carry their own
block ids and source positions, and **click-to-source jumps into the included
file**, not the page that pulled it in. The dev server also watches every
transitively included file, so editing a partial re-renders the pages that use it.

::: {.callout-note}
## The `_includes/` convention

A partial is just a `.qmd` file, but you usually do not want it discovered as its
own page in a site build. Two conventions keep it out of the way: a file (or
folder) whose name starts with an underscore is skipped by the page walker, and the
idiomatic home for shared partials is an `_includes/` directory near the project
root. A nested post then reaches its shared partial with a relative climb, exactly
as the corpus does:

```markdown
{{< include ../../_includes/three-scene.qmd >}}
```
:::

An include that cannot be expanded is **left visible and reported**, never dropped
silently. Three things stop an expansion, each with its own located warning:

| Situation | What happens |
|---|---|
| **Unsafe path** | An absolute path, or one that climbs above the project root (`.git`/`_site.yml` marks the root), is refused: it could read `/etc/passwd` or escape the repo. The directive stays literal and warns "path escapes the project root". |
| **Include cycle** | A file that (directly or transitively) includes itself is refused before it loops. The directive stays literal and warns "include cycle". |
| **Unreadable file** | A missing or unreadable target leaves the directive literal and warns "file not found or unreadable". |

A `{{< include >}}` inside a fenced code block is treated as documentation (this
page relies on that) and is neither expanded nor watched.

## `{{< embed >}}`: a slide deck in an iframe

```markdown
{{< embed talk.qmd >}}
{{< embed talk.qmd title="My conference talk" >}}
```

Embeds another document's deck view inside the current page as a responsive **16:9
iframe**, with a fullscreen button and an "Open ↗" link to view it standalone. The
iframe is deliberate: a deck's full-viewport CSS, keyboard handlers, and JavaScript
are isolated from the host page, so an embedded deck cannot fight the page that
holds it.

| Argument | Required | Default | Effect |
|---|---|---|---|
| *path* (positional) | yes | (none) | The deck source, relative to the embedding page. A `.qmd` path is mapped to its built `.html`; an already-`.html` path is used as written. |
| `title="…"` | no | "Embedded slide deck" | The iframe's accessible name (its `title` attribute), announced by screen readers. |

It emits a `<div class="qmd-embed">` containing the framed `<iframe>` and the
control bar. A deck on a **built-in** theme is theme-aware: an embedded deck
follows the host page's light/dark setting rather than its own. A deck with a
custom or extension `theme:` owns its own colours and is left as-is (no
host-following script is emitted).

::: {.callout-important}
## Embeds need a site build, not a single-doc build

In a **site** build or preview, every deck referenced by an `{{< embed >}}` is
discovered, built, and served as a dependency, yet kept **out of the navigation and
the search index** (it is a component of a page, not a page in its own right). A
**single-document** `build` does **not** build the embedded target (it would not
know where to put it), so it warns and the iframe points at a file that may not
exist. Use a site build, or build the deck yourself alongside the page.
:::

The deck syntax the embed points at is covered in
[Output formats](../using/formats.qmd).

## `{{< video >}}`: a framed screencast

```markdown
{{< video tour.mp4 >}}
{{< video tour.mp4 dark=tour-dark.mp4 poster=tour.jpg caption="A quick tour" >}}
```

Emits a framed `<video>` that **autoplays, is muted, loops, and plays inline**: the
silent-screencast pattern, authored in Markdown so a page never needs raw `<video>`
HTML. It renders as a `<figure class="qmd-video">`.

| Argument | Required | Default | Effect |
|---|---|---|---|
| *src* (positional) | yes | (none) | The video file, relative to the page. A query string is fine: `clip.mp4?v=2` is treated as a path, not a named argument. |
| `dark=…` | no | (none) | A second clip for dark theme. Both clips are emitted; CSS shows the one matching `html[data-theme]`, so the screencast matches the surrounding theme. |
| `poster=…` | no | (none) | A poster image shown before the video paints. |
| `caption="…"` | no | (none) | A `<figcaption>` under the clip (quote it if it has spaces). |

A `{{< video >}}` (and any raw `<video src>`) whose local file is missing is flagged
by `qmd-fast check` as a broken local asset, so a renamed clip does not slip
through.

## `{{< input >}}`: a reactive control

```markdown
{{< input name="k" type="slider" min="1" max="10" step="1" value="3" label="k" >}}
{{< input name="n" type="number" min="0" max="100" value="20" label="n" >}}
{{< input name="on" type="checkbox" value="true" label="enabled" >}}
{{< input name="q" type="text" value="hello" label="query" >}}
{{< input name="c" type="select" options="alpha,beta,gamma" value="beta" label="channel" >}}
```

Emits a labelled, keyboard-accessible control whose value becomes a node in the
[reactive `{js}` graph](../using/interactive.qmd). A `{js}` cell reads it with
`//| input: NAME` and `qmd.value("NAME")`, so you get an input with no
control-building code. It is the same wiring a `//| viewof` cell uses; the control
just carries a `data-qmd-input="NAME"` attribute that the runtime registers.

| Argument | Required | Default | Effect |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name=` | warns if omitted | (none) | The reactive node's name (what a consuming cell reads). Omitting it warns (the control still renders, but it can't feed the reactive graph). |
| `type=` | no | `slider` | One of `slider`, `range`, `number`, `checkbox`, `text`, `select`. An unknown type warns with a did-you-mean. |
| `label=` | no | the `name` | The visible label text. |
| `value=` | no | (none) | The initial value. A `checkbox` is pre-checked only when `value` is the literal `true`; a `select`'s value must exactly string-match one of the `options` to pre-select it. |
| `min=` `max=` `step=` | no | (none) | Numeric bounds for `slider`, `range`, and `number`. |
| `options=` | for `select` | (none) | A comma-separated option list. **Required** for `type="select"`; omitting it warns. |

`slider` and `range` are aliases: both render the same `<input type="range">`
with a live `<output>` readout beside it (only `number` differs, dropping the
readout for a numeric field). `qmd.value()` hands a consuming cell the right type:
a number for `slider`, `range`, and `number`; a boolean for `checkbox`; a string
for `text` and `select`.

The preview stays read-only: a reader moves the control to explore the output, but
the control never writes back to the source. For the full reactive model (how a
change re-runs exactly the cells downstream, in order) see
[Interactive and explorable documents](../using/interactive.qmd).

## Extension-declared shortcodes

An [extension](../using/extensions.qmd) can add its own shortcodes by declaring a
name → HTML-template map in its `_extension.yml`, with no JavaScript:

```yaml
shortcodes:
  youtube: '<div class="ratio"><iframe src="https://www.youtube.com/embed/{{1}}" allowfullscreen></iframe></div>'
  callout: '<aside class="note"><strong>{{title}}</strong> {{body}}</aside>'
```

Once the document activates the extension (with the `extensions:` front-matter
list, or by naming a format extension in `format:`), the declared tags expand
against those templates. Arguments fill the template's placeholders two ways:

- **Positional** bare arguments fill `{{1}}`, `{{2}}`, … in order.
- **Named** `key=value` arguments fill `{{key}}`. Wrap a value in quotes to group
  spaces (`title="Heads up"`).

```markdown
{{< youtube dQw4w9WgXcQ >}}
{{< callout title="Heads up" body="this expanded from a shortcode" >}}
```

An extension may also override a built-in name with its own template (a declared
`embed` or `input` template wins over the built-in one), so the same vocabulary is
fully extensible. See [Extensions](../using/extensions.qmd) for the manifest, the
`{{< … >}}` template syntax, and the client-enhancer API for anything that needs
real interactivity.
